questions.prompt: A point has pixel x1 in image 1. Where must its correct match lie in image 2 (known relative pose, calibrated cameras)?
options: Anywhere in the image, since a single pixel does not constrain its match
On a circle around the principal point whose radius is set by the depth
At the same pixel coordinates as x1 whenever the cameras are calibrated
On the epipolar line determined by x1 and the relative pose
questions.explanation: The ray through x1 projects to a line in the other image, the epipolar line.

questions.prompt: Rectified stereo with f = 600 px and baseline 0.15 m. A feature has disparity 30 px. What is its depth in metres? (precision 0.01)
Same rig (f = 600, B = 0.15 m). First-order depth error for a point at Z = 6 m with a disparity error of 0.5 px, sigma_Z = Z^2 sigma_d/(f B), in metres (precision 0.01)?
A single moving camera recovers the relative pose from the essential matrix. What can it NOT determine?
options: Whether a point lies in front of the camera
The metric length of the translation (scale)
questions.explanation: E and lambda*E satisfy the same constraint; scale needs a known baseline, IMU or object size.

questions.prompt: Two views with baseline 0.3 m of a point at 6 m. What is the parallax angle 2*atan(B/(2Z)) in degrees? (precision 0.01)
The camera only rotates between two frames (translation zero). What happens to triangulation?
options: The essential matrix has full rank and the pose is fully determined
Scale becomes observable, because pure rotation fixes the world unit
The rays are parallel in direction: depth cannot be recovered
Depth is recovered with double accuracy since the rays intersect twice
questions.explanation: With t = 0 there is no baseline and E = 0.

questions.prompt: A robot with two cameras must measure depth to 5% at 6 m. Which design parameters set the achievable accuracy, and what limits making the baseline very large?
rubric: Error sigma_Z = Z^2 sigma_d/(f B): baseline, focal length and disparity noise.
Limits: matching across very different views, occlusions, larger minimum range, mounting and calibration.
questions.explanation: Rubric-guided: compare your answer with each rubric point; this question is not automatically graded.
